discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch. Both assertions now use `should(value)`, which fails on `undefined` instead of short-circuiting. Checked by mutation: with the proto-to-host converter dropping `annotations`, the round-trip test now fails.

Good catch — the code fixtures all carried "overloaded" in the message, so the code check was not covered on its own. Added table-driven cases for each capacity code with a neutral message, plus an unknown code with a neutral message that must stay non-retryable.

Leaving this out on purpose. Counting spawns in a unit test would mean mocking `node:child_process`, which breaks the promisified `execFile` (`.child` / `{ stdout }`), or putting a shell-script `git` wrapper on PATH, which won't work on Windows. We try not to add test-only plumbing like that. The process counts were checked against real checkpoints instead: CLI and VS Code sessions on a repo with 3,000 untracked files. main peaked at 3,051 concurrent git processes and 3,046 zombies for one comparison; this branch uses 6 git processes in total per comparison. The existing tests still cover correctness for both the tracked and the third-parent lookups.

Added `scripts/desktop-startup.test.ts` (`test:sidecar-startup`, wired into the ubuntu sidecar test step in sdk-test.yml): it compiles the real entrypoint, bootstraps an isolated Hub with `--remote-hub-ensure` on an OS-assigned port and a dedicated discovery path, pins the sidecar to that port, and requires the ready line plus a healthy `/health`. It fails with `No compatible hub runtime is available` without the entrypoint fix and passes with it.

agent feedback: The first three recovery tests cover the feature's main promises well: successful retry, truncation again, and nothing to compact. The tests from here onward mostly protect detailed telemetry behavior for listener errors, hooks, empty responses, and tool-call variants that the run loop already owns. If the telemetry contract is simplified to whether compaction/retry completed, I think these extra cases and much of their supporting implementation can be removed while preserving the important behavioral coverage.

Valid — fixed, test-first: both `stop` and `max-tokens` empty retries reproduced exactly this (`Model returned empty response`, truncated turn gone). An empty retry is no more a replacement than an aborted or errored one, so it now keeps the truncated turn and lets the loop surface the max-tokens error, matching the nothing-to-compact path. Also added a table-driven test over the full retry-outcome matrix (every finish reason × text / tool call / empty / provider-executed activity) asserting the partial answer is never silently dropped and the loop is never handed an empty turn — all 20 cells pass.
